summary: Climbing Bukhansan with Grandma, catching your breath, the view from the top, trees and plants, sports talk, and Ji-woo's school sports day.

notes.title: Hiking in Korea
notes.text: Hiking (등산) is a national pastime. On weekends, Seoul's mountains — 북한산, 관악산, 도봉산 — fill with hikers in bright gear, many in their 60s and 70s. Everyone shares snacks on the trail: 김밥, fruit, boiled eggs. -자마자 means "as soon as": 도착하자마자 (as soon as we arrive).

lessons.goal: Explain why you couldn't do something with -느라고.

notes.title: -느라고
notes.text: -느라고 explains that you were busy doing one thing, so you couldn't do another: 일하느라고 밥을 못 먹었어요 (I was working, so I couldn't eat). It's a polite way to say why you missed a call or ran late: 공부하느라고 전화를 못 받았어요.

notes.title: -(으)ㄹ수록
notes.text: -(으)ㄹ수록 means "the more…, the more…": 배울수록 재미있어요 (the more I learn, the more fun it gets). For emphasis, say the verb twice: 보면 볼수록 (the more you look). Ways to say "very": 굉장히, 대단히, 무척, 몹시, 너무나, and casual 되게.

notes.title: Plant words
notes.text: 나무 (tree), 줄기 (trunk, stem), 가지 (branch), 뿌리 (root), 잎 (leaf), 열매 (fruit). Verbs: 심다 (to plant), 가꾸다 (to tend), 따다 (to pick). Persimmon trees (감나무) heavy with orange fruit are a classic sight in Korean yards every autumn.

notes.title: Sports
notes.text: Many sports are borrowed words — 골프, 테니스, 스케이트 — but the big ball games have Korean names: 축구 (soccer), 야구 (baseball), 농구 (basketball), 배구 (volleyball). 씨름 is traditional Korean wrestling, and 태권도 is Korea's national martial art. 경기 = game, 경기장 = stadium, 선수 = athlete.

lessons.goal: Talk about winning, losing and cheering.

scene.en: It's sports day at Ji-woo's school. All the families have come to watch.

scene.ko: 제이미 씨! 저 달리기에서 일등 했어요!
scene.en: Jamie! I came in first in the race!

scene.ko: 와, 챔피언이다! 올림픽 선수 같아!
scene.en: Wow, a champion! You're like an Olympic athlete!

scene.ko: 다음은 줄다리기예요. 우리 팀이 이길 거예요!
scene.en: Next is tug-of-war. Our team is going to win!

scene.ko: 사람들이 손뼉을 치며 응원해요.
scene.en: Everyone claps and cheers.

scene.ko: 아… 졌어요.
scene.en: Oh… we lost.

scene.ko: 괜찮아. 질 때도 있고 이길 때도 있어. 다 같이 박수!
scene.en: That's okay. Sometimes you lose, sometimes you win. Everybody clap!

notes.title: 운동회
notes.text: Every fall, Korean schools hold a sports day (운동회): relay races, tug-of-war (줄다리기), and a blue team against a white team (청팀 vs. 백팀). Parents and grandparents come with lunch boxes to cheer. Cheers: 파이팅! 이겨라! — and lots of 박수.
